Mucosal involvement (oral ulcers) and widespread epidermal necrosis favor SJS/TEN over infectious vesiculobullous processes such as VZV; VZV PCR has been appropriately ordered but the histology points to drug-related epidermal necrolysis. The reported distribution appears limited (upper half of the back), suggesting limited body-surface involvement (<10%), which fits Stevens-Johnson syndrome rather than TEN. Although the patient denies recall of new medications, many causative exposures can be missed. Overall, the combination of acute onset, bullae, desquamation, mucosal ulceration, and biopsy-proven epidermal necrosis makes Stevens-Johnson syndrome the most likely diagnosis.

[DIAGNOSIS]
Stevens-Johnson syndrome (drug‑induced epidermal necrolysis; SJS)
